summary: HUMAN-DATA VALIDATION (CICL causative-verbs, Cao et al. 2023; 72 participants, 7 force-dynamics scenes x 9 verbs): the force model predicts the human proportion-yes across 21 (condition x category) cells with Pearson r = 0.993 [0.987,0.999] (graded), 0.949 (binary, no tuned constants); Spearman rho 0.897; 63-verb-cell r 0.989. Info-free twin (shuffle predictions) mean -0.002 (p95 0.374, beats=True); category-marginal baseline r 0.185 (beaten). The config is decoded from the STIMULUS labels, not the responses, so this is a NON-circular validation of the force-dynamic (necessity, sufficiency) representation against real human causal-verb judgments.

dataset.name: CICL causative-verbs (Cao, Geiger, Kreiss, Icard & Gerstenberg 2023)

brain_note: This validates the PINNED force-dynamic computation (Wolff) + the graded (necessity, sufficiency) read-out against independent human judgments: the affector-necessity + patient-tendency + endstate structure predicts which of CAUSE/ENABLE/PREVENT humans apply, and how strongly. Replaces the near-circular Trabasso-ordinal check with a real, item-level, human-graded target.
scope: Physical force-dynamics scenes (the CORE typing computation), not discourse-level extraction. The config decode is verbatim from the dataset's analysis script. The GRADED variant adds two principled swept discounts (opportunity-not-taken, redundant-prevention); the BINARY variant has none and still beats the twin. Residual: the 'enabled' opportunity reading (enable applies even when the patient chose otherwise) is only half-captured -- a known, honest gap.
